Each face gets 100 N. The defined force is applied uniformly to the selected objects, so a 200 N force load on two faces of equal area is split evenly, with each face loaded with 100 N (implemented via the *CLOAD card in CalculiX).
The FreeCAD FEM ConstraintForce uses the *CLOAD card in CalculiX.

FreeCAD uses Gmsh as the default mesher for creating a FEM mesh. Depending on the OS and installation, Gmsh may be bundled with FreeCAD; if not, install it separately and set its path under Edit → Preferences → FEM → Gmsh.
If Gmsh is not bundled with your FreeCAD installation, install it separately and set the path to gmsh.exe in the menu Edit → Preferences → FEM → Gmsh.

Per the FEM MeshGmshFromShape documentation, you can try: (1) set Data Second Order Linear to true while keeping Data Element Order at 2nd; (2) set Data Element Order to 1st; (3) use a smaller element size by reducing Data Characteristic Length Max. The excerpt also mentions a ccxtools-related note about nodes of nonpositive jacobian elements when using the run button, but the text is cut off.
Elmer does not support Netgen meshes.

Run the single command `ccx` in the terminal. If the solver is correctly installed, you get a simple response such as `Usage: CalculiX.exe -i jobname`. Then make sure the FEM Workbench can find the binary: go to Edit → Preferences → FEM → CalculiX → Search in known binary directories. If you compiled the solver yourself, untick that option and give the correct path to the binary.

The original framework, Solver CalculiX Standard, is preferred because it contains extra checks, for example showing the elements with nonpositive Jacobian, which might cause solution difficulties. The new framework (shared with the Elmer and Z88 solvers) keeps its code hidden from the user.

In FreeCAD 0.21 and below, the self-weight constraint uses a fixed gravity acceleration of 9.81 m/s^2 (written as 9810 mm/s^2 in the CalculiX .inp file). It can only be changed by manually editing the .inp file.
If checked, multiple *.inp files are written and the main input deck uses the *INCLUDE keywords to reference the other ones. If unchecked, a single large *.inp file is written.

The PartDesign Pad tool extrudes a sketch or a face along a straight path. It is invoked from the Part Design → Additive Features → Pad menu or via the Pad button, after selecting a single sketch or one or more faces from the Body.
A positive taper angle tapers the pad in the extrusion direction so that the outer pad border gets wider. The Taper angle option is only available if Type is Dimension.
Through All extends up to the last face of the support it encounters, but for technical reasons it is actually a 10 meter deep pocket. For deeper pockets, use the type Dimension.

The Tip is the PartDesign Feature that is exposed outside the Body: other tools from any workbench (e.g. Part SimpleCopy or Part Cut) use the shape of the Tip, so it is the final representation of the Body as if the parametric history didn't exist. By default it is automatically set to the last feature created in the Body (marked in the Tree View with an overlay icon of a white arrow inside a green circle). It can be changed to an intermediate feature via Set Tip in the Tree View context menu or by changing the Body's Data Tip value.
The Hole feature can create countersink, counterbore, and straight holes. It also supports other parameters such as threading, size, and fit.

Edge numbers are not completely stable. If you add fillets or chamfers before finishing the main solid body, edges could change names (the topological naming problem) and the filleted edges would likely become invalid. Some protection exists when the Data Use All Edges property is true.

Part Extrude always creates a standalone shape, while PartDesign Pad fuses the extrusion result to the rest of the Body. Part Extrude can be placed anywhere in the model tree, whereas PartDesign Pad can only be placed inside a PartDesign Body. Part Extrude can extrude any object with a Part geometry (OpenCASCADE shape) except solids and CompSolids, and it can extrude individual faces of other objects. PartDesign Pad only accepts a Sketch or faces of PartDesign objects as a profile.

Boolean operations are done by the OpenCASCADE Technology (OCCT) kernel, which sometimes has problems producing results when input objects share an edge or a face. To be safe, shapes should intersect clearly (one shape should protrude or be larger than the other). With coplanarity, even if the first boolean succeeds, later booleans may fail, and the real problem may be in older, nested operations shown in the Tree View. Part CheckGeometry is recommended to inspect all objects for problems.

The Sketcher ConstrainLock tool (Lock Position) applies horizontal dimension and vertical dimension constraints to points. If a single point is selected, the constraints reference the sketch origin; if two or more points are selected, they reference the last point in the selection.
A line without constraints has 4 degrees of freedom (DoF): it can be moved horizontally or vertically, stretched, and rotated.
If two lines are selected (or a line and the endpoint of another line), the Sketcher tangent constraint makes the lines collinear. Lines are treated as infinite for this constraint.
FreeCAD macros should have the .FCMacro extension (rather than the .py extension used by standard Python files).

Run the installer from the command line with the /S switch: FreeCAD-~.exe /S. Default settings are used for all options. To set a custom installation path, add /D: FreeCAD-~.exe /S /D=A path to FreeCAD with spaces. Even in silent mode, a short popup appears by default while the installer is checked for corruption.

With HomeBrew installed, run in a terminal: `brew install --cask freecad`. To use the latest version available on HomeBrew, run: `brew install freecad`. Any issues with the HomeBrew Cask or Formula can be reported to the maintainers.

Each FreeCAD object has a Data Placement property, which contains the Data Base (position) and Data Rotation (orientation) of the object. In scripting it is accessed as e.g. box.Placement, with box.Placement.Base for the position.
The Std Measure command gives access to the Unified Measurement Facility, which replaces several previous measurement commands and provides versatile measurement functionality.

For structures, the *BOUNDARY keyword can prescribe temperature, displacements and rotations. (It is also used for gas networks, liquid networks and channels, with other quantities such as mass flow and pressure.)

Degree of freedom 11 stands for temperature. In pure thermal or combined thermomechanical analyses, the *BOUNDARY card for degree of freedom 11 is used to prescribe temperatures (instead of *TEMPERATURE).

Use the *CLOAD card. The excerpts show the data line format as node, direction, magnitude, e.g. `*CLOAD` followed by `4000,1,10.` applies a point force of 10 in direction 1 at node 4000. Behavior across steps: by default, loads from previous steps are kept; specifying a force in a node/direction defined in a previous step replaces that value; a force specified again for the same node and direction within the same step is added to the earlier value; OP=NEW removes all concentrated loads applied in previous steps.

The mass density defined with *DENSITY is required for a frequency analysis (*FREQUENCY), for a dynamic analysis (*DYNAMIC or *HEAT TRANSFER), and for a static analysis with gravity loads (GRAV) or centrifugal loads (CENTRIF). The density can be temperature dependent.

A CalculiX material name (the NAME parameter of *MATERIAL) can contain up to 80 characters. Some models require a specific prefix, e.g. names starting with "SINGLE CRYSTAL" or "ELASTIC FIBER", but the total length limit is still 80 characters.

Use the *FREQUENCY keyword with the number of eigenfrequencies on the second line. For example, *FREQUENCY followed by 10 requests the 10 lowest eigenfrequencies and corresponding eigenmodes. The eigenfrequencies are always stored in jobname.dat. For a rotating model with Coriolis forces, use *COMPLEX FREQUENCY,CORIOLIS followed by 10.

C3D10 is the ten-node tetrahedral element in CalculiX. It is a general purpose tetrahedral element with 4 integration points, and it behaves very well. The C3D20R element yields still better results for the same number of degrees of freedom.

For *STATIC, the default is the first solver that has been installed from this list, in order: SGI, PaStiX, PARDISO, SPOOLES and TAUCS. The SOLVER parameter can be used to select a specific one instead.

No special compilation flag is needed. At execution time, set the environment variable OMP NUM THREADS or CCX NPROC STIFFNESS to the number of cores (default is 1). If both are set, CCX NPROC STIFFNESS takes precedence. The maximum number of cores is detected automatically via sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_CONF) and can be overridden with the environment variable NUMBER OF CPUS.

CalculiX does not use any fixed units: finite element programs do not know any units, so the user must provide numbers with consistent units. For thermomechanical problems four units can be chosen freely, e.g. length, mass, time and temperature. Frequently used systems include SI and mm, N, s, K (and mm, g, s, K). For electromagnetism an additional basic unit, the Ampère (A), is needed, and all other quantities can be written in the SI-units A, m, s, kg and K.

Run a linearized version first: eliminate large deformations (drop NLGEOM), use a linear elastic material, and drop all other nonlinearities such as contact. If the linear version doesn't run, the nonlinear problem won't run either. The linear version also lets you check that boundary conditions are correct (no unrestrained rigid body modes) and that the loading is as intended, and gives a feeling for what the solution should look like. (Separately, rule 1 is to check the mesh quality in CalculiX GraphiX or another good preprocessor.)
On *SOLID SECTION, the parameters ELSET and MATERIAL are required. ELSET defines the element set to which the material specified by MATERIAL applies. ORIENTATION and NODAL THICKNESS are optional.
Each *STEP card must at some point be followed by an *END STEP card, which concludes the definition of the step.
The *BUCKLE procedure is used to determine the buckling load of a structure. For example, *BUCKLE 2 calculates the lowest two buckling modes and the corresponding buckling factors.
